data.one_liner: Unified motion system combining physics-based springs and duration-based curves.
data.what_it_does: Provides a consistent Motion API to handle both physics-based spring animations and duration-based curved animations. It supports multi-dimensional animations, sequence animations, and includes Apple Cupertino and Material Design 3 motion presets.
use_when: You want a mix of physics-based spring animations and curve-based animations under a single API.
You need multi-dimensional animations like Offset or Rect with independent physics per dimension.
You want to use preset Material 3 or Cupertino motion tokens.
avoid_when: You are looking for timeline-based vector animations like Rive or Lottie.
You only need basic, built-in implicit Flutter animations without custom motion configs.
strengths: Unified API for springs and curves
Independent physics simulation per dimension for complex types
Built-in Cupertino and Material Design 3 motion tokens
weaknesses: Requires learning a new motion abstraction over standard Flutter animations
data.setup_notes: Add the package to pubspec.yaml dependencies.

alternatives.name: flutter_animate
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a fluent extension-method based animation API rather than a unified motion system.

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need rich vector animations created in the Rive editor.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need to render After Effects animations exported as JSON.
